# The BigQuery emulator CloudBurrow builds

CloudBurrow's BigQuery is **goccy/bigquery-emulator v0.8.1**, a community emulator (Google
publishes none), **built by CloudBurrow from its source with patches to it and to the SQL engine it links**
(#1061). This directory is everything that build reads besides the Go module proxy; no source
of the emulator or its dependencies is committed here, only the pins and the patches.

## Where each piece comes from

| Module | Version | Commit the tag names | Licence | Changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`github.com/goccy/bigquery-emulator`](https://github.com/goccy/bigquery-emulator) | v0.8.1 | `a531d3deb716eaba4972f9afa88e03e2c0f1a1af` | MIT | twenty-six patches |
| [`github.com/goccy/googlesqlite`](https://github.com/goccy/googlesqlite) | v0.3.1 | `36f6275991c003cde752014fa886eae33df6615d` | MIT (one file Apache-2.0, below) | thirty-nine patches |
| [`github.com/goccy/bigquery-emulator`](https://github.com/goccy/bigquery-emulator) | v0.8.1 | `a531d3deb716eaba4972f9afa88e03e2c0f1a1af` | MIT | twenty-two patches |
| [`github.com/goccy/googlesqlite`](https://github.com/goccy/googlesqlite) | v0.3.1 | `36f6275991c003cde752014fa886eae33df6615d` | MIT (one file Apache-2.0, below) | thirty-six patches |
| [`github.com/goccy/go-googlesql`](https://github.com/goccy/go-googlesql) | v0.3.0 | `eb229fca73e7dca3fc9e8e8be733d14a565f912c` | MIT | two patches |
| every other module the emulator links | v0.8.1's `go.sum` | | each its own | no |

The three MIT licence texts are in [licenses/](licenses/). Each version is v0.8.1's own choice:
[go.mod](go.mod) requires the emulator and nothing else, and its build list for the command
linked is, module by module, the same as v0.8.1's own (checked with `go list -deps`), except that
the three modules above are replaced by the patched copies.

## How it is built and checked

`make bigquery-binaries` (part of `make build` and of each release) runs
[tools/bqengine](../../tools/bqengine), which:

1. downloads each patched module at its version through the go command, which checks it against
   the checksum database, and checks the download's `h1:` hash, and the hash of its files in the
   module cache, against [sources.json](sources.json);
2. copies it to `build/` (not committed) and applies its patches in order, strictly: a hunk that
   does not match its lines exactly fails the build, with no fuzz and no search;
3. checks that [go.mod](go.mod)'s replacements are in force, so a version bump that forgot the
   patches cannot build unpatched;
4. builds `github.com/goccy/bigquery-emulator/cmd/bigquery-emulator` for linux/amd64 and
   linux/arm64 with `CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath -mod=readonly`, every other module fetched and
   checked against [go.sum](go.sum), and the build tag `http2legacy` (golang.org/x/net v0.54.0,
   which v0.8.1 pins, leaves its HTTP/2 server out of a Go 1.27 build without it);
5. writes each binary gzip-compressed, and the licence and notice files of every module linked into
   it, to `internal/bigqueryimage/bin/`, which the CLI embeds, each with a `.inputs` stamp: a hash
   of the pins and patches, the go command that built it, and its architecture. A later run keeps
   a binary whose stamp matches.

`make bigquery-binaries BQENGINE_FLAGS=-prebuilt` builds nothing: it checks that the binaries in
place were built from these sources, by any go command, and fails otherwise. CI builds the
binaries once per workflow run, cached by the same inputs, and its other jobs use them that way;
each release builds them from source once, for its four CLIs (#1087,
[docs/ci.md](../../docs/ci.md#the-embedded-bigquery-emulator)).

`up` then builds `dev.local/cloudburrow-bigquery:<content hash>` from the binary for the node's
architecture on the digest-pinned distroless base the storage image uses, and loads it into kind;
nothing is pulled but that base, and `cloudburrow prefetch` stores the built image for
`up --offline`. The image carries the licence bundle at `/licenses/bigquery-emulator.txt`, and
each release archive carries it as `LICENSES-bigquery-emulator.txt`.

## The patches

Each patch starts with a description of the bug, the CloudBurrow issue, and its licence, and
carries a regression test that fails without it and passes with it, run in the module's copy
under `build/` once `go run ./tools/bqengine -prepare-only` has written it, for example:

```sh
cd third_party/bigquery-emulator
GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly GOWORK=off go test -tags http2legacy github.com/goccy/bigquery-emulator/internal/metadata
```

| Patch | What it fixes | Whose |
|---|---|---|
| [bigquery-emulator 0001](patches/bigquery-emulator/0001-decode-base64-bytes.patch) | A BYTES value streamed, loaded or written from a query's rows was stored as the bytes of its base64 text, so bytes that are not UTF-8 could not be written at all (#1065, #1075) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0002](patches/bigquery-emulator/0002-read-jobs-when-asked-expire-results.patch) | Every request read every job the emulator had run, with its whole result, and each job rewrote the project's list of jobs, so every request got slower with each job (0.27 s for a `SELECT 1` after 40 queries of 50,000 rows); and no result was ever dropped. A job is now read when a request names it, its result only by `jobs.getQueryResults`, and a result is kept up to 24 hours and while the results kept come to 256 MiB (#1086) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0003](patches/bigquery-emulator/0003-empty-repeated-fields.patch) | A REPEATED column a streamed row or a load's record left out was stored NULL, and a null one was refused, where BigQuery writes an empty array (#1124) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0004](patches/bigquery-emulator/0004-bigquery-wkt-text.patch) | A GEOGRAPHY streamed or loaded as WKT text read back as given (`POINT (3 4)`), where BigQuery writes `POINT(3 4)` (#1119) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0005](patches/bigquery-emulator/0005-nested-geography-wkt.patch) | A GEOGRAPHY given as WKT text inside a RECORD or REPEATED column of a streamed row or a load was stored as given (`POINT (1 2)`); it is now written in BigQuery's form at any depth, as 0004 does at the top level (#1138); needs 0001 and 0004 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0006](patches/bigquery-emulator/0006-wkt-number-form.patch) | A GEOGRAPHY given as WKT text kept its numbers as written, POINT(1.0 2), where BigQuery writes POINT(1 2) (#1138); needs 0004, 0005 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0007](patches/bigquery-emulator/0007-index-job-ids.patch) | Each new job checked that its ID was free by reading every job the emulator kept (googlesqlite's comparisons cannot use the primary key), so each query got slower with every job: 500 queries took 3.6 s at first and 5.7 s by 3,000 jobs. Which jobs exist is now kept in memory, and the 500 take 3.0-3.5 s throughout (#1103); needs 0002 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0008](patches/bigquery-emulator/0008-range-schema-and-values.patch) | A RANGE value in a query result had a schema field of no type, which no client could read, and its TIMESTAMP and DATETIME bounds were GoogleSQL text. RANGE columns now have the type RANGE and rangeElementType, and top-level and REPEATED RANGE values are in BigQuery's REST form (#1111) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0009](patches/bigquery-emulator/0009-read-jobs-by-key.patch) | jobs.get, jobs.getQueryResults and each poll of a job's wait read the job with a GoogleSQL WHERE on the jobs table's key, which googlesqlite's comparisons keep SQLite from answering from the key's index, so each read visited every job the emulator kept. One job is now read by its key as SQLite SQL (#1103, #1057); needs 0002 and googlesqlite 0018 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0010](patches/bigquery-emulator/0010-no-read-timeout-on-the-body.patch) | The emulator's server gave each request 15 s in all, its body included, so a load whose data took longer to arrive failed "failed to read csv: ... i/o timeout" (a 5.6 MB multipart upload at 150 KiB/s; a console resumable load on CI). Headers and idle connections keep 15 s; the body has no clock, WriteTimeout's 5 minutes still bound the request (#1192) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0011](patches/bigquery-emulator/0011-save-dataset-updates.patch) | datasets.patch and datasets.update answered the dataset as changed but never wrote it to the metadata store, so a datasets.get afterwards read it as before. The changed metadata is now saved (#1205) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0012](patches/bigquery-emulator/0012-query-error-without-scan-prefix.patch) | A query that failed as it ran, ERROR('boom') among them, failed "failed to scan rows: boom", in jobs.query, a query job's errorResult and a script's @@error.message, where BigQuery gives "boom". The error is now returned as it is (#1230) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0013](patches/bigquery-emulator/0013-times-in-milliseconds.patch) | A table's creationTime and lastModifiedTime, and a job's statistics.creationTime, startTime and endTime, were in seconds since the epoch, where BigQuery gives milliseconds, so the Go client read them as January 1970; a dataset had neither time. All are now milliseconds, and datasets.insert sets a dataset's (#1310) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0014](patches/bigquery-emulator/0014-column-defaults.patch) | A table made by tables.insert with a column's defaultValueExpression had no DEFAULT in the engine, so an INSERT that left the column out wrote NULL; tabledata.insertAll, the Storage Write API and loads never applied a default; and a CREATE TABLE column's DEFAULT did not read back as its defaultValueExpression. A column's default is now its DEFAULT in the engine, a row that does not give the column gets it (a NULL given stays NULL), and a CREATE TABLE column's DEFAULT reads back (#1340); needs googlesqlite 0027 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0015](patches/bigquery-emulator/0015-ingestion-partition-time.patch) | A table made by tables.insert with timePartitioning and no field was made in the engine as any other, so it kept no row's ingestion time. It is now made PARTITION BY TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(_PARTITIONTIME, <its type>), so every write (DML, tabledata.insertAll, loads, the Storage Write API) records each row's, and the pseudo-columns stay out of a CREATE TABLE's schema (#1277); needs googlesqlite 0028 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0016](patches/bigquery-emulator/0016-streaming-buffer-mark.patch) | A table made by tables.insert partitioned by a column (timePartitioning with a field) or an integer range had nothing to mark the rows of its streaming buffer. It is now made with the pseudo-column `_PARTITION_BUFFERED BOOL`, which a CREATE TABLE's schema leaves out (#1273); needs googlesqlite 0029 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0017](patches/bigquery-emulator/0017-list-jobs-in-one-scan.patch) | jobs.list read the project's jobs with a GoogleSQL `id IN UNNEST(@jobIDs)`, a function call per row: 8.7 s for 5,000 jobs, and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS past a minute (#1369). One SQLite scan of the project's rows now; needs 0002, 0009 and googlesqlite 0019 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0018](patches/bigquery-emulator/0018-streamed-at-column.patch) | Nothing kept the time a row was streamed, so DML could not refuse a row streamed in the last 30 minutes. Every table made by tables.insert now has the pseudo-column `_PARTITION_STREAMED TIMESTAMP`, which a CREATE TABLE's schema leaves out (#1370); needs googlesqlite 0030 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0019](patches/bigquery-emulator/0019-quote-struct-field-names.patch) | tables.insert made a RECORD's fields in the engine with their names unquoted, so a field with a flexible column name (`in ner_`, which a Parquet load under `columnNameCharacterMap` `V2` makes) or a keyword failed "Syntax error". The field's name is now quoted, as a column's is (#1373) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0020](patches/bigquery-emulator/0020-round-decimal-columns.patch) | A value written to a parameterized NUMERIC(P, S) or BIGNUMERIC(P, S) column was kept at its full scale, and one past the precision kept. Each time a table's resource is written, and when its engine table is made, SQLite triggers on each such top-level column round what any write path stores by the column's `roundingMode`, else the table's `defaultRoundingMode`, else ROUND_HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO, and refuse a value past the precision OUT_OF_RANGE (#1401); needs googlesqlite 0031 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0021](patches/bigquery-emulator/0021-round-nested-decimal-fields.patch) | Patch 0020 rounded top-level columns only. The same triggers on each column that holds a parameterized NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC STRUCT field or ARRAY element, at any depth, round it by its `roundingMode`, else the table's `defaultRoundingMode`, else ROUND_HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO, and refuse a value past the precision OUT_OF_RANGE (#1409); needs googlesqlite 0032 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0022](patches/bigquery-emulator/0022-list-job-configurations.patch) | jobs.list listed each job without its configuration whatever the projection, so the front read each one it had not seen with a jobs.get: 16.6 s for the first list of 5,000 jobs.query jobs. With `projection=full` each job is now listed with the configuration jobs.get gives (#1419) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0034](patches/bigquery-emulator/0034-front-clock.patch) | Serves `POST /cloudburrow/clock` `{"offsetNanos": n}`, which sets the engine's clock offset (googlesqlite patch 0044), so the front's advanced clock is the engine's too (#1466); needs googlesqlite 0044 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0037](patches/bigquery-emulator/0037-default-time-zone-header.patch) | A request could give the engine no default time zone. The header `X-Cloudburrow-Default-Time-Zone`, which CloudBurrow's front sends with a query of a project that sets `default_time_zone`, now runs the request's queries in that zone (#1456); needs googlesqlite 0047 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0038](patches/bigquery-emulator/0038-csv-empty-string-mark.patch) | A CSV load stored every empty value as NULL, where BigQuery, with a `nullMarker` set, loads an empty value into a STRING or BYTES column as an empty string. One value, U+FDD0 `cloudburrow:empty-string` U+FDD0, which the front writes for such a value, now loads as an empty string (#1457) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [bigquery-emulator 0041](patches/bigquery-emulator/0041-reported-times-by-the-engine-clock.patch) | The emulator stamped the times it reports by the system clock (a dataset's and a table's `creationTime` and `lastModifiedTime`, a job's `startTime` and `endTime`, a Storage API read session's `expireTime`, a write stream's `createTime` and `commitTime`), while since 0034 CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() and the change history read the engine's, which follows CloudBurrow's front's. Each is now stamped by the engine's clock, `googlesqlite.Now` (#1487); needs 0034 and googlesqlite 0051 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0001](patches/googlesqlite/0001-cast-nested-struct-fields-upstream-pr-76.patch) | A RECORD inside a REPEATED RECORD, streamed or loaded, left the table unreadable ("failed to convert struct from array") (#900) | **Not CloudBurrow's**: goccy/googlesqlite pull request [#76](https://github.com/goccy/googlesqlite/pull/76), by Masaaki Goshima (@goccy), the project's author, at its head `63e6793e1f7994d80e40bc3b976fac1889aaebf0`, unchanged; open upstream, under the project's MIT licence |
| [googlesqlite 0002](patches/googlesqlite/0002-keep-table-function-handles-alive.patch) | A garbage collection freed a table function the catalog still used, and its next call trapped or crashed the emulator, losing every dataset (#1043, #1047) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0003](patches/googlesqlite/0003-drop-table-function.patch) | `DROP TABLE FUNCTION` was refused ("Statement not supported: DropTableFunctionStatement"), so a table function could not be dropped or replaced (#976, #986) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0004](patches/googlesqlite/0004-keep-nan.patch) | Every FLOAT64 NaN read back NULL: SQLite turns a NaN it is bound, or that a function returns, into NULL (#1066); and an infinity inside an ARRAY or a STRUCT failed "json: unsupported value" (#1077) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0005](patches/googlesqlite/0005-unary-minus.patch) | `-a` of anything but a literal failed "no such function: googlesqlite_unary_minus" | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0006](patches/googlesqlite/0006-bare-path-sub-catalogs-upstream-pr-80.patch) | Every catalog rebuild (each DROP of a table, view or function) registered the whole builtin function set again into each project's and dataset's sub-catalog, in WebAssembly memory that only grows (#1057, #1017) | **Not CloudBurrow's**: goccy/googlesqlite pull request [#80](https://github.com/goccy/googlesqlite/pull/80), by @cp-ant, at its head `fc357c6e11c02f7f9ddc52a940e82bc50039bcb3`, unchanged but for its hunk's line numbers; open upstream, under the project's MIT licence |
| [googlesqlite 0007](patches/googlesqlite/0007-functions-of-every-dataset.patch) | With a default dataset, a call of another dataset's SQL function or table function failed "no such column: <project>": only the default dataset's were inlined (#1107, #1123) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0008](patches/googlesqlite/0008-function-by-one-quoted-path.patch) | A function or table function named by one quoted path (`` `project.dataset.fn`(x) ``) was "Function not found" (#1122) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0009](patches/googlesqlite/0009-interval-signs-and-sub-second-parts.patch) | A negative INTERVAL of less than an hour was written, stored and read back positive; `INTERVAL n MILLISECOND` and `MICROSECOND` were refused (#1126) | CloudBurrow's: MIT, and Apache-2.0 for its change to `internal/intervalvalue/intervalvalue.go`, which googlesqlite copied from cloud.google.com/go/bigquery (Copyright 2022 Google LLC) |
| [googlesqlite 0010](patches/googlesqlite/0010-interval-comparison.patch) | `=`, `<` and the other comparisons of two INTERVALs failed "unsupported eq operator for interval value" (#1120); needs 0009 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0011](patches/googlesqlite/0011-null-arguments.patch) | Functions that panicked (the emulator answering 500) or failed on a NULL argument; IN and IN UNNEST FALSE where a comparison with NULL decides (#1109, #1121) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0012](patches/googlesqlite/0012-bigquery-wkt.patch) | A GEOGRAPHY was written `POINT (1 2)` and an empty one `POINT EMPTY`, where BigQuery writes `POINT(1 2)` and `GEOMETRYCOLLECTION EMPTY` (#1119) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0013](patches/googlesqlite/0013-typed-json-encoding.patch) | TO_JSON_STRING and TO_JSON did not follow GoogleSQL's JSON encodings: a BOOL read from a table was `1`, a DATE, DATETIME, TIME or TIMESTAMP was unquoted (not JSON), a fractional or wide NUMERIC, a wide INT64, an infinity or NaN, an INTERVAL and a RANGE were written otherwise than the table says (#1116) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0014](patches/googlesqlite/0014-json-builders-typed-values.patch) | JSON_OBJECT, JSON_ARRAY, JSON_SET, JSON_ARRAY_APPEND and JSON_ARRAY_INSERT wrote a BOOL read from a table as `1` and a DATE, DATETIME, TIME or TIMESTAMP unquoted (not JSON), and JSON_SET of a DATE failed; their values now take TO_JSON's encoding (#1127); needs 0013 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0015](patches/googlesqlite/0015-nan-sort-order.patch) | A FLOAT64 NaN sorted after +inf in ORDER BY and in an aggregate's ORDER BY, where BigQuery sorts NULL, NaN, -inf ... +inf (#1089); needs 0004 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0016](patches/googlesqlite/0016-free-parser-options.patch) | Every statement parsed leaked its parse tree in the engine's WebAssembly memory (parser options made with no finalizer), so the emulator grew with every query job and request: 159 to 989 MiB over 3,500 small queries, flat at about 300 MiB with the patch (#1133, #1057, #1103) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0017](patches/googlesqlite/0017-collect-before-catalog-rebuild.patch) | Each DROP rebuilds the root catalog with every builtin function, and the catalog it replaced was freed only by a finalizer after a Go collection, which the engine's large WebAssembly memory put off, so the memory grew at every DROP: 120 CREATE+DROP pairs, 237 to 603 MiB. A collection now runs before each rebuild: 169 to 171 MiB (#1057, #1103) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0018](patches/googlesqlite/0018-tables-and-functions-of-one-name.patch) | A table named as a function of its dataset (legal in BigQuery: separate namespaces) overwrote the function's row in the engine's catalog store, and from then on every DROP panicked "nil pointer dereference" and the table functions were lost until a restart; functions and table functions now have rows of their own (#1186) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0019](patches/googlesqlite/0019-read-rows-by-key.patch) | Every GoogleSQL WHERE comparison is a function call SQLite cannot answer from an index, so a keyed read visits every row. Adds `Conn.QueryRawContext`, `EncodeString` and `DecodeString`, for a caller that knows a table's stored encoding to read a row by its key as SQLite SQL; nothing googlesqlite does itself changes (#1103, #1057) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0020](patches/googlesqlite/0020-one-ast-walk-per-statement.patch) | Each statement's parse tree was walked five times before it was analyzed, each node several WebAssembly calls: 36% of an INSERT ... VALUES of 2,000 rows. One walk now: 10,000 to 16,000 rows/s by jobs.query on the native emulator (#1070) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0021](patches/googlesqlite/0021-naive-timestamps-utc.patch) | A TIMESTAMP with no time zone was read in America/Los_Angeles, the analyzer's default, not UTC as BigQuery reads it: TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01', CAST('2020-01-01' AS TIMESTAMP) and RANGE<TIMESTAMP> literal bounds. A date alone, RANGE<TIMESTAMP> bounds and CAST('...' AS TIMESTAMP) strings with no zone now get the UTC offset; a CAST of a DATE, DATETIME or TIMESTAMP literal is still folded in the default zone (#1188, #1189) | CloudBurrow's, MIT
| [googlesqlite 0022](patches/googlesqlite/0022-default-time-zone-utc.patch) | The analyzer folded a CAST of a literal, and coerced a literal, in its default zone, America/Los_Angeles, not BigQuery's UTC: CAST(DATE/DATETIME literal AS TIMESTAMP), CAST(TIMESTAMP literal AS STRING/DATE/DATETIME/TIME), TIMESTAMP = '<string>'. Its default zone is now UTC (with go-googlesql 0002). A TIMESTAMP column cast to STRING was RFC 3339, STRING(ts, zone) always said "+00", and a STRING with a named zone could not be cast to TIMESTAMP at run time (#1189) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0023](patches/googlesqlite/0023-cast-format.patch) | CAST's FORMAT clause and AT TIME ZONE were dropped: CAST(x AS STRING FORMAT '...') ignored the format and CAST('...' AS DATE/DATETIME/TIME/TIMESTAMP/BYTES FORMAT '...') failed or ignored it. BigQuery's documented format elements now work for BYTES to and from STRING, DATE/DATETIME/TIME/TIMESTAMP to and from STRING (a TIMESTAMP in the AT TIME ZONE zone, else UTC) and INT64/FLOAT64/NUMERIC/BIGNUMERIC to STRING; anything else is an error (#1194, #1195) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0024](patches/googlesqlite/0024-cast-to-string-forms.patch) | A column cast to STRING at run time used the wire form, not BigQuery's: DATETIME had a T ("2018-12-03T15:30:00"), DATETIME, TIME and INTERVAL sub-second digits were not in groups of three, FLOAT64 NaN and infinities were "NaN"/"+Inf"/"-Inf", and BYTES were base64. They now match the analyzer's folding of a literal, which is BigQuery's (#1202) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0025](patches/googlesqlite/0025-unnest-infinity.patch) | UNNEST of an array holding an infinite FLOAT64 failed "json: unsupported value: +Inf": googlesqlite_decode_array wrote the elements into JSON as bare doubles. An infinity now goes in the value envelope there too, as patch 0004 does inside an ARRAY or STRUCT (#1204) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0026](patches/googlesqlite/0026-int-float-comparisons.patch) | An INT64 compared with a FLOAT64 truncated the float to an int64: 2 = 2.5 was true, and an infinity became MinInt64 on amd64 and MaxInt64 on arm64, so MAX over an UNNEST of [+Inf, 2.0] answered 2 on amd64 (#1235). Compared as FLOAT64, as BigQuery does. | `value_int_float_compare_test.go`; `inf_unnest_test.go` on linux/amd64 |
| [googlesqlite 0027](patches/googlesqlite/0027-column-defaults.patch) | A column's DEFAULT applied only to an INSERT ... VALUES that left it out: INSERT ... SELECT left it NULL, and the DEFAULT keyword in VALUES failed "no formatter registered for ResolvedNodeKind ResolvedNodeKindResolvedDmldefault". Both now write the default, and the catalog keeps the DEFAULT's text (#1340) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0028](patches/googlesqlite/0028-ingestion-partition-time.patch) | `_PARTITIONTIME` and `_PARTITIONDATE` were rewritten as CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() and CURRENT_DATE() on any table. A CREATE TABLE partitioned by ingestion time now gets them as pseudo-columns (left out of SELECT *) whose DEFAULT is the insert's time truncated to the unit, `_PARTITIONDATE` only by day, and a table without them fails "Unrecognized name" (#1277); needs 0027 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0029](patches/googlesqlite/0029-streaming-buffer-mark.patch) | A table partitioned by a column or an integer range had no way to tell a row of its streaming buffer from the others. A CREATE TABLE with a column list and a PARTITION BY that is not ingestion time now gets the pseudo-column `_PARTITION_BUFFERED BOOL` (left out of SELECT *; an INSERT may give it), which CloudBurrow's front sets on a streamed row and clears at the flush; BigQuery reserves the prefix `_PARTITION` for column names (#1273); needs 0028 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0030](patches/googlesqlite/0030-streamed-at-column.patch) | A column named `_PARTITION_STREAMED` is now a pseudo-column (left out of SELECT *; an INSERT may give it), the time CloudBurrow's front streamed the row, which DML reads to refuse a row streamed in the last 30 minutes; a CREATE TABLE with a column list (not TEMP) gets the column too; BigQuery reserves the prefix `_PARTITION` for column names (#1370); needs 0029 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0031](patches/googlesqlite/0031-round-decimal.patch) | Adds the SQLite function `googlesqlite_round_decimal` (a NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC rounded to a scale by ROUND_HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO or ROUND_HALF_EVEN, OUT_OF_RANGE past a precision) and `RawSQLitePrefix`, which runs a statement as SQLite SQL, for the emulator's rounding triggers (#1401) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0032](patches/googlesqlite/0032-round-decimal-nested.patch) | Adds the SQLite function `googlesqlite_round_decimal_nested`, which rounds the NUMERIC and BIGNUMERIC values a spec names inside an encoded STRUCT or ARRAY, at any depth, as `googlesqlite_round_decimal` rounds one, for the emulator's rounding triggers (#1409) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0035](patches/googlesqlite/0035-interval-arithmetic.patch) | INTERVAL + INTERVAL failed "unsupported add operator for interval value", as did -, * INT64, / INT64 and unary minus; DATE '2021-01-31' + INTERVAL 1 MONTH was 2021-03-03; JUSTIFY_* changed their argument and left mixed signs; EXTRACT read uncanonical parts. Arithmetic part by part (months, days, nanoseconds) with GoogleSQL's range errors (#1437) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0036](patches/googlesqlite/0036-change-history.patch) | Gives every `project.dataset.table` a CREATE TABLE makes a change table, `table$changes`, of each row inserted, deleted and updated, with `_CHANGE_TYPE`, `_CHANGE_TIMESTAMP` (the transaction's time) and `_CHANGE_IS_FOR_UPDATE`, filled by SQLite triggers, so every write path is recorded; kept seven days; left out of wildcards and INFORMATION_SCHEMA; the front reads it for `APPENDS` and `CHANGES` (#1418) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0041](patches/googlesqlite/0041-change-row-identities.patch) | Gives every change table (patch 0036) the pseudo-columns `googlesqlite_change_micros`, `googlesqlite_change_rowid` (the changed row's rowid) and `rowid` (the order of the changes), which `SELECT *` leaves out, and a `_CHANGE_TYPE` 'START' row of when it was made; the front reads `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF` a past time from them (#1460) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0044](patches/googlesqlite/0044-replaced-history-and-clock.patch) | CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE started the table's change table (patch 0036) over, so the replaced contents were lost to time travel, `APPENDS` and `CHANGES`; it now carries the old history into the new change table, with a DELETE of each replaced row at the time of the replace. And the engine's clock (`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()` and the change times) takes an offset, `googlesqlite.SetClockOffset`, so it reads the front's clock (#1466) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0047](patches/googlesqlite/0047-default-time-zone-of-a-query.patch) | The engine knew one time zone, UTC, so a project's `default_time_zone` reached only what the front could write into the query text. `WithDefaultTimeZone` gives a query a zone that every call taking one and given none uses where its argument resolves to TIMESTAMP (DATE, DATETIME, TIME, STRING, EXTRACT, the `*_TRUNC`, FORMAT_/PARSE_TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMP(), CURRENT_DATE/DATETIME/TIME), as do casts between TIMESTAMP and STRING, DATE, DATETIME or TIME, and TIMESTAMP literals with no zone; literal casts are left unfolded for such a query (#1456); needs 0021, 0022 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0049](patches/googlesqlite/0049-struct-float-type.patch) | A whole FLOAT64 (3.0) in a STRUCT field or an ARRAY element was encoded as the JSON integer 3 and read back as an INT64, so `s.x / 2` was 1 and `s.x * 0.5` was 0; it is written with a fraction, and INT64 arithmetic with a FLOAT64 operand, and INT64 `/`, are FLOAT64 (#1484) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [googlesqlite 0051](patches/googlesqlite/0051-catalog-times-by-the-engine-clock.patch) | The catalog stamped a table's, view's and function's creation and update times by the system clock, so INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES' `creation_time` read another clock than CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), as did the year a CAST ... FORMAT without one defaults to and UNIX_TIMESTAMP(). They now read the engine's clock (0044), and `googlesqlite.Now` gives that clock to the emulator (#1487); needs 0044 | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [go-googlesql 0001](patches/go-googlesql/0001-unsigned-wasm-addresses.patch) | Once the engine's WebAssembly heap passed 2 GiB, every call panicked "slice bounds out of range", addressing it with signed 32-bit offsets (#989) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |
| [go-googlesql 0002](patches/go-googlesql/0002-utc-time-zone.patch) | The bindings could not build a TimeZone, so the analyzer's default zone could not be set; adds UTCTimeZone() (#1189) | CloudBurrow's, MIT |

Nothing here has been filed or proposed upstream; whether to is the maintainer's decision (#974).
When an upstream release carries a fix, drop its patch and bump the pin in sources.json, go.mod,
dependencies.json and `internal/bigqueryimage.Version` together; `go test ./tools/bqengine
./internal/bigqueryimage` fails while they disagree.
